issues.description: The problem text first instructs that the SealSaloon.stock should be initialized in the constructor (implying an instance final field) but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static. This is a structural contradiction about whether 'stock' is an instance final field initialized in the constructor or a static shared field. Students may be confused about whether to declare stock as non-static final and set it in the constructor or as a static final initialized at declaration.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design: either (A) require a non-static final Stock stock initialized in the no-arg constructor (and remove the note that stock must be static), or (B) require a static final Stock stock shared across all SealSaloon instances (and remove the instruction to initialize it in the constructor). Update the problem statement (and UML if needed) to consistently state the chosen approach. If (B) is intended, explicitly say 'declare stock as static final and initialize at declaration or in a static block.'

issues.description: The problem specification and UML refer to a checkOrderReady() method (used by orderMeal and described in the behavior), but the provided reference solution implements this logic in a method named processOrders(). This name mismatch between the required API (checkOrderReady) and the solution's public method may confuse students about the expected method name and signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align names in the materials: either rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() (and keep its behavior), or update the problem statement/UML to refer to processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady(). Ensure the method name in the specification, template instructions, and reference solution match exactly so students implement the expected API.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon that is invoked after placing an order to attempt serving queued orders. The solution implementation provides this behavior under a differently named method processOrders(). This name divergence for the same core behavior (processing/checking whether queued orders can be served) creates a mapping confusion for students who will look for or be asked to implement checkOrderReady() but find processOrders() in the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name for this behavior across artifacts. Rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() (and ensure orderMeal() calls checkOrderReady()), or update the problem statement to require processOrders() instead. Prefer renaming processOrders() -> checkOrderReady() to match the problem description.
